title: Architecture Patterns with Python
access: Complete author-hosted HTML book available under CC BY-NC-ND; only the specified chapters were read. No book text, diagrams, or example code redistributed.
read_sections: Chapter 6: complete main text, examples, trade-offs, recap and footnote, author HTML lines 24–430.
Chapter 7: complete main text, examples, trade-offs, recap and footnotes, author HTML lines 24–523. Embedded diagram source inspected; not every rendered diagram independently verified.

findings.trigger: A Python use case performs several database writes.
findings.failure: Persistence operations commit independently or leak transaction lifetime into handlers.
findings.mechanism: Name one transaction owner and make success, rollback and release paths explicit; prefer the existing ORM boundary when sufficient.
findings.conditions: The writes share one transactional authority. Context-manager syntax alone establishes neither isolation nor remote atomicity.
findings.counterexample: A successful payment followed by database rollback is still a successful payment.
findings.verification: Force an error between writes and observe final persisted state through a fresh connection on the production database engine.

findings.trigger: Concurrent Python handlers enforce an aggregate invariant.
findings.failure: Both handlers validate an old state and commit incompatible changes.
findings.mechanism: Identify the common database conflict point and enforce the invariant there; use controlled interleavings to test it.
findings.conditions: Every relevant writer participates. The chapter's PostgreSQL example relies on Repeatable Read, not just incrementing a field.
findings.counterexample: Two Read Committed writes setting an unconstrained version field to the same value need not conflict.
findings.verification: Force read/read/write/write ordering; assert business state and transaction outcomes. Compare against the actual database isolation contract.

limitations: The full book was available, but it was not read in full.
Examples reflect the book's framework era. Use installed ORM APIs and versioned database documentation.
The existing concurrency-correctness skill owns distributed invariant diagnosis; this source adds Python persistence implementation detail.
The chapter itself qualifies sleep-based race tests and recommends synchronization primitives. Preserve that qualification.

title: Effective Python: 125 Specific Ways to Write Better Python
edition: Third edition; print publication November 20, 2024; copyright 2025
access: Publisher supplies Chapter 5 in HTML and an 80-page sample PDF including frontmatter, Chapter 5 and index. The complete book was not accessed. Public searches did not establish an authenticated freely accessible full copy.
read_sections: Publisher/author edition metadata and full table of contents inspected; ISBN 9780138172183 verified in publisher sample.
Complete Chapter 5 Items 30, 32, 36, 37 and 38 read in publisher HTML: argument mutation, failure results, dynamic defaults, parameter kinds and decorator metadata.
PDF frontmatter, contents and selected matching item passages inspected. This is not a complete Chapter 5 reading.

findings.trigger: Request handling accepts mutable arguments or creates dynamic defaults.
findings.failure: Shared defaults or aliases leak state between calls.
findings.mechanism: Make mutation ownership explicit and initialize per-call state inside the call.
findings.conditions: Use a distinct sentinel if None is meaningful; shallow copies still share nested objects.
findings.counterexample: Copying a request dictionary leaves its nested list shared.
findings.verification: Call twice with separate requests and inspect nested state, identity and timestamps.

findings.trigger: A backend helper exposes failure, flags or a decorator.
findings.failure: Falsey success becomes failure, flags swap, or wrappers obscure the interface.
findings.mechanism: Model outcomes explicitly, name ambiguous options and preserve wrapper metadata.
findings.conditions: Preserve supported callers; metadata preservation does not make a synchronous wrapper asynchronous.
findings.counterexample: Zero is a valid result; an optional lookup may legitimately return None.
findings.verification: Exercise zero/empty success, expected failure, existing call forms and introspected signatures.

limitations: Coverage through Python 3.13 is the author's declared scope; current free-threaded builds and structured-concurrency behavior need official documentation.
Robustness and concurrency chapter titles were inspected, not their complete prose. Runtime guidance in the companion report is attributed to official Python documentation instead.
Book examples and copyright remain with their owners; proposed fixtures must be original.

title: Effective TypeScript: 83 Specific Ways to Improve Your TypeScript
access: Author-hosted complete sample items, example repository and edition announcement. Full second-edition text not accessed; generic full-PDF search results were not treated as authenticated editions.
read_sections: Complete author sample Item 74, Chapter 9: runtime types, three schema strategies and trade-offs.
Complete author sample Item 36, Chapter 4: special values and explicit variants.

Complete author article published May 31, 2023, titled Item 30: documentation/type duplication. The second-edition repository lists this topic as Item 31; it is not represented as an authenticated second-edition excerpt.
Second-edition repository table of contents and TypeScript 5.4.5 sample-checking baseline inspected.

findings.trigger: A TypeScript service accepts external input.
findings.failure: Assertions or generated types are mistaken for validation.
findings.mechanism: Use one schema authority for runtime validation and static types, with generation drift checked when applicable.
findings.conditions: Match the existing contract/toolchain; shape checks do not establish authorization or business validity.
findings.counterexample: A schema listing properties without required accepts their omission.
findings.verification: Reject missing/wrong-type fields, test the extra-field policy, and run compilation separately from execution.

findings.trigger: A response can be pending, absent, failed or successful.
findings.failure: In-band sentinel values enter ordinary calculations.
findings.mechanism: Represent distinct outcomes as explicit variants and exhaustively handle them.
findings.conditions: Enable appropriate null checking and preserve valid zero/empty values.
findings.counterexample: An unknown amount encoded as -1 is processed as a refund.
findings.verification: Add a variant and require the compiler to expose unhandled branches; exercise every runtime state.

findings.failure: Prose becomes stale while code evolves.
findings.mechanism: Keep rationale, units, errors and effects in prose; keep checked shapes in types.
findings.conditions: Readonly is a static access restriction, not deep runtime freezing.
findings.counterexample: Deleting a timeout-unit comment removes information absent from number.
findings.verification: Review documentation against the contract and preserve behavior-relevant information.

limitations: The runtime-types article's illustrative generated schema omits required. Treat examples as teaching material and verify the generated artifact's actual acceptance behavior.
Current compiler/runtime versions must be discovered in the target repository rather than inherited from 2024 sample tooling.
Do not import the author's personal schema-library preference as a universal requirement.

title: Learning Go: An Idiomatic Approach to Real-World Go Programming
access: Published second-edition metadata, table of contents, short publisher previews and author example code. No complete second-edition prose chapter accessed. Author site's free generics chapter explicitly belongs to revised first edition. Third edition is unfinished, with publisher date April 2027.
read_sections: Publisher second-edition TOC and Chapter 14 opening context explanation; Chapters 9, 13 and 15 preview availability checked.

Complete author Chapter 12 sample files: backpressure/main.go, context_cancel/main.go, pipeline/ABProcessor.go, pipeline/CProcessor.go, pipeline/main.go, time_out/main.go, at commit 08720ea422a3c0f0076ed6efc11147687f47163d.
Complete author Chapter 14 sample files: cancel_http/main.go, nested_timers/main.go, own_cancellation/main.go, at commit 71878380fe1c02a872f55fdba65ed44ac7ef997b.

findings.trigger: A Go handler starts work that can outlive its caller.
findings.failure: Returning a timeout is mistaken for stopping the worker.
findings.mechanism: Give each goroutine an owner, cancellation path and completion signal; propagate deadlines into blocking operations.
findings.conditions: Cancellation is cooperative. Buffered result delivery prevents one blocked send but cannot stop arbitrary work.
findings.counterexample: The time_out example calls a worker without passing its context.
findings.verification: Cancel before result consumption and observe all owned workers finish without residual effects.

findings.trigger: An admission token limits concurrent requests.
findings.failure: A recovered panic bypasses ordinary token release.
findings.mechanism: Release acquired capacity through a guaranteed cleanup path.
findings.conditions: Panic recovery belongs at a deliberate boundary; do not convert arbitrary failures into success.
findings.counterexample: In the sample Process method, release occurs after the callback.
findings.verification: After a panicking callback is recovered by its owner, the next request can acquire capacity.

findings.trigger: A Go service repeatedly calls another HTTP service.
findings.failure: Response bodies accumulate even though cancellation is wired.
findings.mechanism: Close every acquired body within its iteration; select an explicit bounded consumption policy.
findings.conditions: Avoid function-wide deferred accumulation inside an unbounded loop.
findings.counterexample: The cancel_http sample does not close successful response bodies.
findings.verification: Instrument a test transport and verify body close on success, rejection and early cancellation.

limitations: Findings about examples are direct code review, not claims about unseen surrounding chapter prose.
The examples were read, not executed. The verification descriptions are proposed evaluations.
Current context, net/http and testing documentation establishes API behavior; the published book predates testing/synctest's stable API.
Do not substitute an unverified full-book mirror or first-edition sample for second-edition reading provenance.
